clue.text: Term applied to some shares down 1p? Check inside

indicators.note: inside is used loosely here to bring the check in alongside the penny letters, joining them in one word

parts.note: feeling down is feeling blue
ch is the chess abbreviation for check
the digit 1 read as the letter I, plus p

explanation.surface: A note on shares that have dropped a penny, with a reminder to check the details within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like falling share prices, but it means sad. The placing word is loose: the check abbreviation sits in front of the one-and-penny letters, not within them.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue-chip is the stock-market label for shares in large, reliable, well-established companies.

clue.text: Black, wild cat in spring

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
the ounce is the snow leopard

explanation.surface: A black wild cat out and about in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' suggests the season, but it is the verb meaning to leap.
explanation.definitionFit: To bounce is to spring up or rebound, the same leaping motion.

clue.text: Complete agreement in marriage about son

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: a marriage is a union
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A married couple in full accord about their son.
explanation.definitionFit: Unison means perfect concord, everyone acting or speaking together.

clue.text: Author, one entering into agreements

indicators.note: entering into means going inside, so the one is placed within the word for agreements

parts.note: charters are formal written agreements or grants
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A writer who signs up to contracts.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes between CHARTER and its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Leslie Charteris was the novelist who created Simon Templar, the Saint.

clue.text: Film in Ecuador and Mali, possibly

indicators.note: possibly hints at one of several arrangements the letters could take

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A film shot on location in Ecuador and Mali, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Irma la Douce is the 1963 Billy Wilder film starring Shirley MacLaine and Jack Lemmon.

clue.text: Goddess entering this gutted ancient city

indicators.note: a gutted word has had its insides removed, leaving only its two end letters
entering means going into, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: the word this with its middle letters removed
Hebe is the Greek goddess of youth

explanation.surface: A goddess makes her way into a ruined ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: HEBE goes between the T and S left from 'this'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes was a major city of ancient Egypt, and also of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Leading actor sank at sea after onset of hurricane

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its start, so only its first letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of hurricane

indicators.note: at sea means confused and adrift, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A star sank in the sea after a hurricane struck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the H in front of the reordered letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Hanks is a leading Hollywood star, a lead actor in many films.

clue.text: Exclamation made by singer when first disc is released

indicators.note: releasing something lets it go, so the first ring-shaped letter is let go

parts.note: Boy George, the Culture Club singer
O is disc-shaped

explanation.surface: A singer cries out when his first record comes out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disc' looks like a record release, but it is the round letter O, the first of which is dropped from the singer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: By George! is an old-fashioned exclamation of surprise or emphasis.

clue.text: Knocks up, then thrashes hardy fellows

parts.note: to spar is to exchange practice blows, like a tennis knock-up
to tan someone's hide is to thrash them

explanation.surface: A man knocks someone about, then thrashes them.
explanation.walkthrough: A knock-up is a practice session, as in tennis, so knocks up suggests sparring; to tan someone's hide is to beat them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spartans were famed for austerity and toughness, so spartan types are hardy fellows.

clue.text: Outraged at university, fashionable members

parts.note: a student in residence at university is said to be up
what is fashionable is in
arms are limbs, members of the body

explanation.surface: A complaint that a university has become a hotbed of trendy members.
explanation.walkthrough: Going up to university is the British idiom for attending it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be up in arms is the idiom for being angrily protesting, i.e. outraged.

clue.text: Cipher worked out in game

indicators.note: worked out suggests letters being processed and rearranged into a solution

parts.note: the six letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A secret code cracked during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked out' reads like solving the cipher, but it rearranges the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Enigma was the German wartime cipher machine, and an enigma is a puzzle or riddle.

clue.text: Blow caught ruffian

parts.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a lout is a rough, uncouth fellow

explanation.surface: A thug is struck by a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: A clout is a heavy hit with the hand, a blow.

clue.text: Left old Stowe novel and newspaper in Suffolk resort

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new arrangement

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
the place name taken as written
the FT is the Financial Times

explanation.surface: Leaving an old book by Stowe and a newspaper behind at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book, especially beside an author's name (Harriet Beecher Stowe), but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowestoft is a seaside town on the Suffolk coast in eastern England, the most easterly in Britain.

clue.text: Method used to clear a bar shown in cowboy film reel

definitions.text: Method used to clear a bar

parts.note: a cowboy film is a western
a roll of film is a reel

explanation.surface: A bar-room brawl filmed on a reel for a cowboy movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a saloon in a western, but it is the high-jump bar.
explanation.definitionFit: The western roll is a high-jump technique, rolling sideways over the crossbar.

clue.text: Guard in round eight's knocked out

indicators.note: something knocked out of shape is battered into a different form

parts.note: all eleven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A boxer knocked out in the eighth round.
explanation.walkthrough: The boxing picture hides the fodder: the letters of 'round eight's' rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride shotgun was to sit beside a stagecoach driver as an armed guard; the verb means to guard.

clue.text: In a row to do with article written by radical?

parts.note: on means concerning, to do with
the definite article
Trot is short for Trotskyist, a left-wing radical

explanation.surface: An article on a quarrel, penned by a political extremist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel, but here it means a sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: On the trot is British idiom for consecutively, one after another without a break.

clue.text: Standing still, deer stalked by worker after noon

indicators.note: after says the worker comes behind the noon letter, so it is written second

parts.note: a stag is a male deer
N is the abbreviation for noon
the worker ant is the usual crossword worker

explanation.surface: A deer freezes while being hunted by a labourer in the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'stalked by' puts what follows below the deer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnant water is still and not flowing; the word means motionless.

clue.text: Island's local drink, first of beverages to be served up

parts.note: a local is a neighbourhood pub, a bar

indicators.note: the first of a word is just its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of beverages

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means turned upwards, so the drink reads from bottom to top

parts.note: soda is a fizzy drink

explanation.surface: An island pub serving its home-brewed drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A local is British slang for one's nearby pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbados is a Caribbean island nation.

clue.text: Shining through, managed cryptic clues in first of Torquemada books

indicators.note: in places the managed part inside the outer letters
'first of' keeps only the first letter of 'Torquemada'

parts.note: the opening letter of Torquemada

indicators.note: cryptic means obscure or coded, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
taken as written
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Torquemada, the famous Observer setter, managing cryptic clues in his books.
explanation.walkthrough: Torquemada was a legendary Observer crossword setter, so the surface is a crossword in-joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Translucent describes material that lets light pass through it, though not clearly.

clue.text: See figure of importance right away

indicators.note: right away means the right is taken away, so that letter goes

parts.note: stature is standing, importance
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Look at an important person, immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' sounds like immediately, but it removes R from the word for importance.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a sculpted figure set up for people to look at.

clue.text: Mean boy to become a clergyman

parts.note: par is the average or mean level
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A nasty boy decides to join the clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like nasty, but it is the noun for an average.
explanation.definitionFit: A parson is a parish priest or vicar, a clergyman.

clue.text: Agent's good order went out around end of June

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters wrap the June letter
out suggests being put out of order, so those letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Order of the British Empire
taken as written

indicators.note: 'end of' keeps only the last letter of 'June'

parts.note: the final letter of June

explanation.surface: An agent's orders were carried out by the end of June.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British honour, an order of chivalry. The letters of 'went' are reordered as TWEN with E placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-between is an intermediary who carries messages for others, an agent.

clue.text: This may be present in Austen's Emma

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A remark about something that may appear in Jane Austen's novel Emma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like being there, but it is the grammatical present.
explanation.definitionFit: Present is one grammatical tense, alongside past and future.

clue.text: Artist on way out? One being ignored more

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so the artist is written second
something ignored is left out, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: an exit is a way out
the Roman numeral for one
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A painter about to leave, overlooked once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artist on way out' sounds like a painter departing; RA is a Royal Academician.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, as in more of something.

clue.text: Burning, forest close to coast

parts.note: the Forest of Arden in Warwickshire, setting of As You Like It

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of coast

explanation.surface: A forest fire burning near the coastline.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means passionate, figuratively burning with feeling.

clue.text: Philosopher reacts so unexpectedly

indicators.note: unexpectedly means in a surprising way, so the letters fall into a surprising order

parts.note: the eight letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A thinker responds in a surprising way.
explanation.definitionFit: Socrates was the classical Athenian philosopher.

clue.text: Sample taken from plant after end of shift

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: the final letter of shift
the aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: A cutting taken from a plant when a gardener's shift ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the plant behind the T.
explanation.definitionFit: A taster is a small sample of something given to try it out.

clue.text: Untidy woman, nurse, gulping coffee

indicators.note: gulping means swallowing, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: SRN is a State Registered Nurse
a latte is a milky coffee

explanation.surface: A scruffy woman, a nurse, gulping down her coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: SRN, State Registered Nurse, is an old British nursing qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: A slattern is an old, disparaging word for a dirty, slovenly woman.
